content.title: About
content.content: White chili (Capsicum annuum) is a variety of hot pepper with a pale‑green, almost white skin. It has moderate heat, a fruity aroma and a slightly sweet aftertaste. White chili is used fresh, dried, pickled, and in sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from its almost colorless skin that fades as the fruit matures.
Capsaicin levels are usually lower than in red varieties, but still enough to add noticeable heat.
The pepper belongs to the nightshade family and is a close relative of sweet bell peppers.
In traditional Mexican cuisine white chili is often used in chilaquiles sauce and fish marinades.
Seeds of white chili can be saved for planting new plants.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains capsaicin
items.content: Capsaicin has antioxidant properties and may boost metabolism.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B6 and folate help nerve function and metabolism.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: One fresh pepper contains less than 30 kcal, making it a diet‑friendly addition.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: Potassium and magnesium in the pepper support blood pressure regulation and muscle function.

items.title: Mucous membrane irritation
items.content: Capsaicin can cause burning sensations in the mouth and stomach, especially in large amounts.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals may develop skin rash or swelling when exposed to pepper.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Capsaicin may enhance the effect of anticoagulants, so caution is advised for users of such medication.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: White chili can be eaten fresh in salads, added to soups, sauces and marinades. Dried peppers are used for powders and seasonings. To reduce heat, remove the seeds and membranes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh white chili in the refrigerator in a plastic bag for up to 1 week. Keep dried peppers in an airtight container in a cool, dry place for up to 6 months.
